title: Assessment of scaling and corrosion potential of drinking water resources of Iranshahr
author: Taghavi, Mohammadi, et al.
materials: To calculate the corrosion indices, 36 samples of 1.5 l volume were collected from 18 sources, stored and transferred to lab according to standard method (stored in a dark cold box (4 °C) and transferred to laboratory within less than 3 h). The pH measured by pH meter device and water temperature determined by thermometer at the sampling points. Water quality parameters such as electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, pH, calcium hardness, and alkalinity were measured in water samples in laboratory upon arriving samples. Alkalinity and hardness were determined using titration method and total dissolved solids was determined by gravimetric method. Sulfate was measured based on turbidity measurement at 420 nm by DR5000 spectrophotometer [1]. The equation of corrosion indices and their interpretations were summarized in Table 1. steps.title: Collect water samples
steps.instruction: Collect 36 water samples of 1.5 L each from 18 sources following the standard method.

steps.title: Store and transport samples
steps.instruction: Place the samples in a dark cold box kept at 4 °C and transfer them to the laboratory within 3 hours.

steps.title: Measure field pH and temperature
steps.instruction: At each sampling point, measure pH with a pH‑meter and water temperature with a thermometer.

steps.title: Analyze water quality parameters
steps.instruction: In the laboratory, determine electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, calcium hardness, alkalinity, and sulfate in the received samples.

substeps.instruction: Measure electrical conductivity directly with an EC meter.
Determine total dissolved solids by gravimetric method.
Determine calcium hardness and alkalinity by titration method.
Measure sulfate by turbidity at 420 nm using a DR5000 spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Calculate corrosion indices
steps.instruction: Compute Langelier, Ryznar, Puckorius, and Aggressive indices using the equations in Table 1 and record the results in Microsoft Excel 2010.
